interface.title: Simulation Decomposition Dashboard (SimDec), with a companion 'Data generation (sampling)' app
interface.field: Uncertainty quantification and global sensitivity analysis of computational models (engineering, environmental and decision models)
interface.stage_of_work: Analysis and reporting of Monte Carlo simulation results, plus designing the sample before the simulation is run
interface.what_it_is_for: Load a table of model inputs and outputs, rank inputs by Sobol-style sensitivity indices, then split the output distribution into colour-coded scenarios made from combinations of the most influential inputs' states, and export the results as CSV.

data.note: The dashboard opens on the bundled stress.csv (output delta_sig; inputs Kf, sigma_res, Rp0.2, R). I also uploaded CO2.csv (output CO2, 8 inputs) and crying.csv (output 'thresh p_hungry', 6 inputs). Both were detected and analysed automatically. The sampling app makes its own synthetic samples and needs no file.

tree.general: Find out which uncertain inputs drive a model's output, describe the output as interpretable scenarios, and report it
tree.specific: Run SimDec on a Monte Carlo input/output CSV: sensitivity indices, then decomposition into scenarios, then a coloured histogram or boxplot, then a CSV export

features.name: Driver picker with live explained-variance readout
features.general: Pick a subset of candidate explanatory factors from a pre-ranked list and see at once how much of the outcome's variation that subset accounts for. The tool proposes a default subset from the top-ranked factors, with a coverage target and a cap on its size.
features.specific: 'Select inputs for decomposition' tag box: auto-filled with the top inputs needed to reach 80% of the summed indices, at most 4 (so CO2.csv got 4 inputs at only 0.64). Add inputs from the dropdown or remove them with x, and 'Explained variance ratio from selected inputs' updates along with the chart and tables.
steps: Read the auto-selected inputs and their explained variance ratio
Open the dropdown and add another input
Remove an input with its x button
Compare the ratio and the resulting scenarios, and keep the best set
serves_tasks: Choose which inputs define the scenarios and check how much variance they explain

features.name: Scenario-coloured distribution chart with view switcher
features.general: Show one outcome's distribution split into groups, as a stacked histogram or as one boxplot per group, with adjustable bin count and axis range
features.specific: Visualization buttons Stacked histogram / Boxplot, with Number of bins (spinner and slider) and X-lim (two spinners and a range slider) that redraw the matplotlib figure
steps: Pick Stacked histogram or Boxplot
Set the number of bins
Narrow or reset the x-axis range
serves_tasks: Compare a stacked histogram with a boxplot of the scenarios

features.name: Group-colour pickers with shade families
features.general: Give each top-level category a base colour. Its sub-groups get shades of it automatically, and the same colours are used in the chart and the legend table.
features.specific: 'Main color for states' pickers (low/medium/high, or low/high when an input has two states). Changing one recolours every scenario that has that state of the first decomposition input, in both the histogram or boxplot and the Scenarios table colour swatches.
steps: Open the Main color for states card
Set a new colour for one state
Check the chart's shade family
Check that the scenario table swatches match
serves_tasks: Restyle the figure colours for publication

features.name: Two-variable scatter with stacked marginal histograms
features.general: Plot two outcome variables against each other, coloured by group, with stacked marginal histograms on both axes, a subsampling control for dense data, and independent axis limits
features.specific: '2 outputs' mode: Second output dropdown, a scatter coloured by scenario with stacked histograms on top and side, 'Share of data shown' (0-1), and X-lim and Y-lim range controls
steps: Press 2 outputs
Choose the second output variable
Lower Share of data shown to thin the points
Set X-lim and Y-lim to zoom into a region
serves_tasks: Plot the outcome against a second variable, coloured by scenario

features.name: Hierarchical scenario summary table
features.general: List every combination of factor levels as a nested table, with a colour key and summary statistics for each, plus a companion table of the value range behind each level
features.specific: Scenarios table, with merged row headers per decomposition input (low/medium/high), N°, colour swatch, std, min, mean, max and probability, and row highlight on hover. 'Details on inputs' states' gives each state's min and max.
steps: Run a decomposition
Read the nested state combinations and their colour swatches
Hover a row to highlight it
Look up each state's value range in the states table
serves_tasks: Read each scenario's statistics and the value ranges that define each input state

features.name: Sortable importance table with inline bars
features.general: Rank factors by an importance score, with an inline bar for each, a total row, and sorting by column
features.specific: Sensitivity Indices grid (Inputs, Indices bar, Value) with a 'Sum of Indices' row. Clicking a header sorts by that column; the Sum of Indices row is sorted along with the data rows instead of staying pinned (bottom when ascending, top when descending).
steps: Load data so the indices are computed
Read the bars and values
Click the Value header to re-sort
Use the ranking to choose decomposition inputs
serves_tasks: See how much of the output variance each input explains
Choose which inputs define the scenarios and check how much variance they explain

features.name: CSV upload with automatic variable roles
features.general: Upload a results table and have the tool guess the outcome column and the explanatory columns, then let the user override them
features.specific: The Choose File (.csv) upload fills the Output dropdown and the Inputs multi-select and re-runs the analysis. Choosing a different Output moves the old one into Inputs, and Ctrl-clicking Inputs leaves columns out.
steps: Press Choose File and pick a CSV
Check the detected Output and Inputs
Switch the Output column if needed
Ctrl-click to leave out irrelevant inputs
serves_tasks: Choose the outcome variable and which inputs to analyse

features.name: Quasi-Monte Carlo design explorer with discrepancy metric
features.general: Generate a space-filling sample on the unit hypercube for several variables, show it as a pair plot, and compare sampling methods with a uniformity score (per-variable distributions and bounds had no effect in this run)
features.specific: /sampling: Number of variables, Number of samples, and Sampling method (Sobol', Halton, Latin Hypercube) feed a corner pair plot (histograms on the diagonal, scatters below) and the 'Discrepancy' value under Metrics
steps: Set the number of variables
Set the number of samples
Switch the sampling method
Compare the pair plot and the discrepancy value
serves_tasks: Choose how many uncertain variables the sample covers
Compare sampling designs by how evenly they fill the space

features.name: One-click bundled results export
features.general: Save the importance scores, the pairwise-interaction matrix, the scenario table and the state-range table together as one CSV file
features.specific: Header Download button saves simdec.csv: unlabeled index blocks in the order si, first_order, second_order (pairwise matrix), then the scenario table (decomposition input columns, N°, colour as integer index, std, min, mean, max, probability) and the state table (variable, state, min, max)
steps: Run a decomposition with the chosen inputs
Press Download in the header
Open simdec.csv and identify the index blocks by their order
Map the integer colour indices back to the on-screen scenario colours
serves_tasks: Save the importance scores, scenario table and state table as a file
